title: Barriers and Facilitators of Parent-Child Communication in Children With Cancer Predisposition
official: Barriers and Facilitators of Parent-Child Communication in Children With Cancer Predisposition
summary:
Children, adolescents, and young adults who have a genetic change that increases their risk of cancer may not fully understand what their genetic test results mean. Parents and caregivers may also find it difficult to talk with their child about cancer risk, cancer screening, and ways to help detect cancer early. This study will examine how parents and young people communicate about inherited cancer risk, what factors help or hinder these conversations, and how these discussions relate to understanding cancer risk and recommended follow-up care. The study will also explore parents' understanding of their child's genetic test results and gather feedback about resources that may help families talk about inherited cancer risk.

Primary Objective(s):

* Identify qualities of parent-CAYA (child, adolescent, and young adults) communication about CAYAs' genomic cancer risk, and their association with CAYAs' psychosocial and prevention outcomes.
* Examine the association between sociodemographic, cancer-related, and psychosocial factors and parent-CAYA communication regarding CAYAs' genomic risk for cancer.
* Identify barriers and facilitators of parent-CAYA communication regarding CAYAs' genomic risk for cancer.

Secondary Objective(s):

\- Examine the association between parents' genetic knowledge, genetic literacy, self- efficacy, and accuracy of cancer predisposition knowledge and their perception of understanding their child's genetic test results.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patient aged 12 to 24 years (inclusive)
* Patient underwent germline genetic testing with a Pathogenic/Likely Pathogenic (P/LP) variant in a known cancer predisposition gene that increases risk for developing cancer
* P/LP result disclosed to the patient
* Patient and participating caregiver able to speak and read English

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patient is only a carrier of a recessive variant that does not alone increase risk for cancer
* Inability or unwillingness to give informed consent/assent
* Participating caregiver is under the age of 18 years
* Patient or participating caregiver has evidence of significant cognitive deficits (per medical record) that would interfere with the ability to comprehend study questions
* Patient's medical status or condition precludes completion of study (as determined by medical team, patient, or parent)
